subject: estimating parameters for several models in sequence

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: estimating parameters for several models in sequence
parts:
Hi,

The problem I am having is solving several models in stan.  There are two independent data sets Y1=model1(x,theta1)+eps1 and Y2=model2(x,theta1,theta2)+eps2 where both eps1 and eps2 are normal. One way is to solve both models simultaneously in stan.  However, it might be easier to estimate theta1 for the first data set Y1 in stan, approximate theta1 estimates via normal in R, transfer means and sigmas of theta1 to a different stan code which estimates theta2 using the second data set Y2 and means/sigmas for theta1.  Is this approach reasonable.  Currently I have stan code to estimate theta1 and theta2 simultaneously (basically by having one loop for the first data set (m_SR) and another loop for the second data set (m).

Thanks for any suggestions,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] estimating parameters for several models in sequence
parts:
> On Apr 14, 2015, at 2:38 AM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> The problem I am having is solving several models in stan. There are two independent data sets Y1=model1(x,theta1)+eps1 and Y2=model2(x,theta1,theta2)+eps2 where both eps1 and eps2 are normal. One way is to solve both models simultaneously in stan. However, it might be easier to estimate theta1 for the first data set Y1 in stan, approximate theta1 estimates via normal in R, transfer means and sigmas of theta1 to a different stan code which estimates theta2 using the second data set Y2 and means/sigmas for theta1. Is this approach reasonable.

I don't think so. What would happen is that you'd be using the
*approximate* posterior for theta1 in model1 as a prior for model2
if I understand you correctly.
> Currently I have stan code to estimate theta1 and theta2 simultaneously (basically by having one loop for the first data set (m_SR) and another loop for the second data set (m).

This is actually a coherent model to estimate theta1 and theta2 jointly,
where theta1 is a paramter of both models.

It would also make sense to estimate the two models independently from
scratch.

- Bob

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] estimating parameters for several models in sequence
parts:
Thanks Bob.  Yes, I estimated both models independently.  Theta1 estimates were similar. 
Thank you,
Linas
